title: Framing Empirical Facts and Policy Debates with El hecho de que

sections.content: You know *el hecho de que* (agreed in the singular with *el hecho*, never *el hecho que*) from B2 Unit 6, past subjunctive sequence of tenses (*quería que vinieras*) from B1 Unit 38, *queísmo* from C1 Unit 2, and negated inferences (*no significa que*) from C1 Unit 8. In academic prose and higher-education policy, *el hecho de que* turns an already verified finding into the grammatical subject or theme of a sentence so that the writer can evaluate it or deny an unwarranted conclusion.

Even though the underlying fact is real, Spanish normally puts the verb inside *el hecho de que* in the subjunctive because the clause is presented as a presupposed background theme rather than a new assertion (*El hecho de que la matrícula aumente...*, *El hecho de que se haya ampliado la licenciatura...*). Remember two C1 syntactic rules: first, the main verb agrees in the singular with *el hecho* (*preocupa*, *exige*, *no significa que*), never with a plural noun inside the subordinate clause; second, when the main clause denies a consequence (*no significa que*, *no implica que*), the second *que* clause also takes the subjunctive.

sections.title: Thematic Evaluation with El hecho de que
rows: El hecho de que la docencia exija más recursos preocupa al decano.
El hecho de que aumentara la deserción estudiantil obligó a revisar el ingreso.
Denying a false inference (*no significa que* + subj.)
El hecho de que un curso sea optativo no significa que tenga menos valor académico.
Prepositional framing (*Pese al hecho de que*)
Pese al hecho de que el campus cuente con aulas nuevas, faltan becas.

items.spanish: El hecho de que muchos jóvenes se matriculen en esta licenciatura confirma el prestigio de la facultad.
items.english: The fact that many young people enrol in this undergraduate degree confirms the faculty's prestige.

items.spanish: El hecho de que una asignatura sea optativa no significa que los estudiantes puedan descuidar la lectura.
items.english: The fact that a course is elective does not mean that students can neglect the reading.

items.spanish: Al rector le preocupaba el hecho de que la deserción aumentara durante el primer semestre.
items.english: The rector was concerned by the fact that the dropout rate increased during the first semester.

items.spanish: El hecho de que el posgrado combine teoría y práctica favorece la formación de los nuevos investigadores.
items.english: The fact that the postgraduate programme combines theory and practice favours the training of new researchers.

sections.content: Never omit *de* in *el hecho de que* (writing *el hecho que* is *queísmo* and is rejected in formal prose), and keep the main verb singular to match *el hecho*: *El hecho de que existan varias becas ayuda a las familias* (not *ayudan*).
